questions.q: What is a baby cat called?
questions.x: Kittens are born blind and deaf, and open their eyes after about one to two weeks.

questions.q: What is a baby dog called?
questions.x: Puppies sleep up to 18 to 20 hours a day while they grow.

questions.q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
questions.x: A newborn joey is about the size of a jellybean and crawls into its mother's pouch.

questions.q: Which animal is known as the king of the jungle?
questions.x: Despite the nickname, lions mostly live in grasslands and savannas, not jungles.

questions.q: Which bird is famous for being unable to fly and living in Antarctica?
questions.x: Penguins use their wings as flippers to swim fast underwater.

questions.q: What do pandas mainly eat?
questions.x: A giant panda can eat 26 to 84 pounds of bamboo every day.

questions.q: Which animal has a long trunk?
questions.x: An elephant's trunk has tens of thousands of muscle units and can lift heavy logs or pick up a single peanut.

questions.q: Which animal is the tallest in the world?
questions.x: A giraffe has the same number of neck bones as a human: seven.

questions.q: What do you call a baby frog?
questions.x: Tadpoles breathe with gills and later develop lungs and legs as they become frogs.

questions.q: What is a baby cow called?
questions.x: A calf can usually stand within an hour of being born.

questions.q: What is a baby horse called?
questions.x: Foals can stand and walk within a few hours of birth.

questions.q: What is a baby sheep called?
questions.x: Lambs can recognize their mother's call within a few days of birth.

questions.q: What is a baby pig called?
questions.x: Piglets are born with sharp teeth, which breeders often notice at birth.

questions.q: What is a baby goat called?
questions.x: Goat kids can walk within minutes of being born.

questions.q: What is a baby bear called?
questions.x: Bear cubs are born tiny, often weighing less than a pound, while their mothers hibernate.

questions.q: Which sea creature has eight arms?
questions.x: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood.

questions.q: What type of animal is a dolphin?
questions.x: Dolphins breathe air through a blowhole and nurse their young with milk.

questions.q: What type of animal is a penguin?
questions.x: Penguins are birds with dense, waterproof feathers, even though they cannot fly.

questions.q: Which animal lays the biggest egg of any living bird?
questions.x: An ostrich egg weighs about three pounds, roughly the same as two dozen chicken eggs.

questions.q: What do caterpillars turn into?
questions.x: Inside the chrysalis or cocoon, the caterpillar's body is almost completely reorganized.

questions.q: Which animal produces honey?
questions.x: A honeybee makes only about a twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its whole lifetime.

questions.q: Which large cat has black stripes on orange fur?
questions.x: Every tiger's stripe pattern is unique, like a human fingerprint.

questions.q: Which animal is known for carrying its home on its back?
questions.x: A snail's shell grows with it and is made of calcium carbonate.

questions.q: Which animal is the fastest on land over short distances?
questions.x: A cheetah can reach about 60 to 70 miles per hour in short bursts.

questions.q: What is the name for a female chicken?
questions.x: A hen can lay about 250 to 300 eggs a year in good conditions.

questions.q: What is a male deer called?
questions.x: Bucks grow and shed a new set of antlers each year.

questions.q: Which animal has black and white stripes?
questions.x: No two zebras have exactly the same stripe pattern.

questions.q: Which animal is known for changing color to blend in with surroundings?
questions.x: Chameleons also change color to communicate mood and regulate temperature.

questions.q: Which animal sleeps hanging upside down in caves?
questions.x: Bats can lock their feet in a gripping position so they hang without using muscle effort.

questions.q: What do cows eat?
questions.x: Cows are ruminants with a four-part stomach that helps them digest plants.

questions.q: Which bird is known for its colorful tail feathers fanned in display?
questions.x: Only the male peafowl, the peacock, has the dramatic train of feathers.

questions.q: Which bird is known for hooting at night?
questions.x: Owls can rotate their heads about 270 degrees.

questions.q: Which animal is known as man's best friend?
questions.x: Dogs were domesticated from wolves at least 15,000 years ago.

questions.q: What is a group of lions called?
questions.x: A pride is often made up of related females, their cubs, and a few adult males.

questions.q: What is a group of wolves called?
questions.x: A wolf pack is usually a family: a breeding pair and their offspring.

questions.q: What is a group of fish called?
questions.x: Swimming in schools helps fish avoid predators and find food.

questions.q: What is a group of cows usually called?
questions.x: Cattle in a herd form social bonds and have preferred companions.

questions.q: What is a group of birds flying together often called?
questions.x: Flying in a flock can save energy and gives more eyes to watch for danger.

questions.q: Which sea animal has a hard shell, claws, and walks sideways?
questions.x: Crabs walk sideways because of how their legs' joints bend.

questions.q: Which animal is known for its black-and-white fur and for living in bamboo forests of China?
questions.x: Giant pandas live in a few mountain ranges in central China.

questions.q: Which animal is the largest living species of bear that lives in the Arctic?
questions.x: A polar bear's skin is black under its translucent, hollow-looking fur.

questions.q: Which sea mammal is known for its tusks and lives in the Arctic?
questions.x: Walrus tusks are elongated canine teeth and can grow over three feet long.

questions.q: Which animal is a monotreme that lays eggs and has a duck-like bill?
questions.x: Male platypuses have venomous spurs on their hind legs.

questions.q: Which animal hops and carries its young in a pouch?
questions.x: A kangaroo cannot walk backward easily, which is one reason it appears on Australia's coat of arms.

questions.q: Which animal eats mainly eucalyptus leaves?
questions.x: Koalas sleep around 18 to 22 hours a day because eucalyptus gives little energy.

questions.q: Which insect is known for building hills and living in a colony with a queen?
questions.x: Some ant colonies have millions of individuals working together.

questions.q: Which insect glows in the dark on summer nights?
questions.x: Fireflies are actually beetles that make light through a chemical reaction.

questions.q: Which animal is the national bird symbol of the United States?
questions.x: The bald eagle's head is not actually bald; the name comes from an older meaning of 'white-headed'.

questions.q: Which reptile has a hard shell and can pull its head inside?
questions.x: A turtle's shell is part of its skeleton, fused to its ribs and spine.

questions.q: Which reptile has no legs and moves by slithering?
questions.x: Snakes smell by flicking their forked tongues to collect scent particles.

questions.q: What sound does a cow make?
questions.x: Cows have regional 'accents' in their moos, according to some farm studies.

questions.q: Which animal gives us wool?
questions.x: Sheep have been raised for wool for at least 8,000 years.

questions.q: What color are flamingos, mostly?
questions.x: Flamingos get their pink color from pigments in the algae and shrimp they eat.

questions.q: Which animal is known for its very long neck and spotted coat in the African savanna?
questions.x: A giraffe's tongue can be up to about 20 inches long.

questions.q: Which sea creature has a star-shaped body?
questions.x: Starfish, properly called sea stars, can regrow lost arms.

questions.q: Which sea creature has stinging tentacles and a bell-shaped body with no brain?
questions.x: Jellyfish are about 95 percent water and have existed for hundreds of millions of years.

questions.q: Which large shark is famous for a dorsal fin that appears in the movie Jaws?
questions.x: Great whites can detect tiny electrical fields from prey using special pores.

questions.q: Which fish is known for its striped orange body and living in anemones, like Nemo?
questions.x: Clownfish have a mucus coating that protects them from the anemone's stings.

questions.q: Which insect makes silk to build a cocoon and is raised for fabric?
questions.x: A single silkworm cocoon can be unwound into a thread nearly a mile long.

questions.q: Which animal spends its life in trees, moves very slowly, and hangs upside down?
questions.x: Algae sometimes grow in a sloth's fur, giving it a greenish tint.

questions.q: Which primate is the closest living relative of humans, along with the bonobo?
questions.x: Humans and chimpanzees share about 98 to 99 percent of their DNA.

questions.q: What is a male lion known for having?
questions.x: A darker, fuller mane often signals a healthier, stronger male.

questions.q: What is a female pig called?
questions.x: A sow can have two litters a year, each with ten or more piglets.

questions.q: What is a female sheep called?
questions.x: Ewes usually give birth to one or two lambs in spring.

questions.q: What is a female horse called?
questions.x: A mare carries her foal for about 11 months.

questions.q: Which animal is the national symbol of Australia, seen on its coat of arms with the emu?
questions.x: Both animals were chosen because neither can easily move backward.

questions.q: Which animal says 'quack'?
questions.x: Ducks have waterproof feathers thanks to oil from a gland near the tail.

questions.q: Which animal makes webs to catch its food?
questions.x: Spider silk is stronger than steel of the same thickness.

questions.q: What do herbivores eat?
questions.x: Cows, rabbits, and elephants are all herbivores.

questions.q: What do we call animals that eat only meat?
questions.x: Cats and hawks are examples of animals built for a meat-based diet.

questions.q: What do we call animals that eat both plants and meat?
questions.x: Bears, pigs, and humans are omnivores.

questions.q: What is the process called when some animals sleep through winter?
questions.x: During hibernation, an animal's heart rate and body temperature drop dramatically.

questions.q: What is it called when birds travel long distances each year to warmer places?
questions.x: Arctic terns migrate from the Arctic to Antarctica and back each year.

questions.q: Which animal is a pet that purrs and chases mice?
questions.x: Cats purr at a frequency of roughly 25 to 150 hertz.

questions.q: Which huge dinosaur had a long neck and ate plants, like Brachiosaurus?
questions.x: Sauropods were the largest land animals ever to walk the Earth.

questions.q: Which dinosaur is famous for its giant head and tiny arms and is often called the 'tyrant lizard king'?
questions.x: T. rex had a bite force among the strongest of any land animal ever.

questions.q: Which dinosaur had three horns on its face and a large bony frill?
questions.x: Its name means 'three-horned face'.

questions.q: Which dinosaur had bony plates along its back and spikes on its tail?
questions.x: Stegosaurus had a brain about the size of a lime.

questions.q: Which extinct hairy relative of the elephant lived during the Ice Age?
questions.x: Woolly mammoths lived alongside early humans and survived on Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago.

questions.q: What do we call scientists who study fossils of ancient life?
questions.x: Paleontologists learn about dinosaurs from fossilized bones, eggs, and footprints.

questions.q: Which animal's milk is used to make most of the cheese and butter in stores?
questions.x: A dairy cow can produce more than 6 gallons of milk a day.

questions.q: Which animal is the largest member of the cat family?
questions.x: Siberian tigers can weigh over 600 pounds.

questions.q: Which animal gives a black ink-like cloud to escape predators?
questions.x: The ink also dulls a predator's sense of smell.

questions.q: Which animal builds dams out of sticks and logs?
questions.x: Beaver teeth never stop growing, and orange enamel makes them extra hard.

questions.q: Which animal can regrow its tail if it is lost?
questions.x: Many lizards detach their tail on purpose to escape a predator.

questions.q: Which sea animal is a mammal and sings long songs underwater, with a hump on its back?
questions.x: Male humpbacks sing complex songs that can last for 10 to 20 minutes.

questions.q: What is the main food of a hummingbird?
questions.x: Hummingbirds can flap their wings dozens of times per second and even hover.

questions.q: Which animal is covered in sharp quills for protection?
questions.x: A porcupine can have around 30,000 quills.

questions.q: Which animal is known for storing fat in one or two humps in the desert?
questions.x: A camel can drink over 30 gallons of water in about 15 minutes.

questions.q: What is a female deer called?
questions.x: Does usually give birth to one or two spotted fawns in late spring.

questions.q: What is a male chicken called?
questions.x: Roosters are known for crowing at dawn, but they can crow at other times too.

questions.q: Which animal is the largest living land animal?
questions.x: A big male African elephant can weigh about 6 tons.

questions.q: In the fable, which animal beats the hare in a race?
questions.x: The tale of the tortoise and the hare is attributed to Aesop.

questions.q: What is a baby duck called?
questions.x: Ducklings can swim within hours of hatching.

questions.q: What is a baby hen or rooster called when it first hatches?
questions.x: A chick starts peeping inside the egg a day or so before hatching.

questions.q: What color is a polar bear's fur?
questions.x: Each hair is actually clear and hollow; it only looks white because it scatters light.

questions.q: What gas do fish take from the water through their gills?
questions.x: Gills pull dissolved oxygen out of water as it flows over thin, blood-rich filaments.

questions.q: Which flightless bird lives in Antarctica?
questions.x: Penguins use their wings as flippers for swimming in the icy sea.

questions.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.x: Two hearts pump blood through the gills and one pumps it around the body.

questions.q: Which sea animal has eight arms and can squirt ink?
questions.x: An octopus squirts a cloud of ink to confuse predators while it escapes.

questions.q: What is a group of crows called?
questions.x: Crows are among the smartest birds and can recognize individual human faces.

questions.q: What is a group of owls called?
questions.x: The term likely comes from the owl's long association with wisdom.

questions.q: What is a group of whales called?
questions.x: Orca pods can last for generations, led by older females.

questions.q: What is a group of flamingos called?
questions.x: Flamingos gather in huge groups, sometimes numbering in the thousands.

questions.q: What is a group of baboons or monkeys on the move often called?
questions.x: A baboon troop can include anywhere from a few dozen to over a hundred individuals.

questions.q: What is a baby swan called?
questions.x: Cygnets are often gray or brownish, becoming white as they mature.

questions.q: What is a baby goose called?
questions.x: Goslings can walk, swim, and feed themselves within a day of hatching.

questions.q: What is a baby pigeon called?
questions.x: Both parents feed squabs with a nutrient-rich 'crop milk'.

questions.q: What is a baby echidna or platypus called?
questions.x: Both echidnas and platypuses are egg-laying mammals called monotremes.

questions.q: What is a baby alpaca or llama called?
questions.x: A cria usually weighs 15 to 20 pounds at birth and can stand within an hour.

questions.q: What is a baby hedgehog called?
questions.x: Hoglets are born with soft, white spines under the skin that harden soon afterward.

questions.q: What is a baby beaver or rabbit commonly called?
questions.x: Baby rabbits are born blind and hairless in a nest lined with their mother's fur.

questions.q: Which bird can fly backward?
questions.x: Hummingbirds rotate their wings in a figure-eight pattern to hover and fly backward.

questions.q: Which marsupial is native to Tasmania and is known for a loud screeching sound?
questions.x: A Tasmanian devil's bite is among the strongest of any mammal relative to its size.

questions.q: Which ocean animal is the only mammal to have a tusk-like spiraled tooth, often called the 'unicorn of the sea'?
questions.x: The tusk is a long canine tooth that can reach about 10 feet.

questions.q: What is the only mammal capable of true flight?
questions.x: Flying squirrels and gliders only glide; bats flap their wings to fly.

questions.q: Which animal's fingerprints are so similar to a human's they can confuse crime scene investigators?
questions.x: Koalas evolved human-like fingerprints independently, a case of convergent evolution.

questions.q: What is the term for animals that are active mainly at night?
questions.x: Owls, bats, and many cats are nocturnal and have adaptations for dim light.

questions.q: What is the term for animals that are most active at dawn and dusk?
questions.x: Rabbits and many deer species are crepuscular.

questions.q: Which mammal lays eggs?
questions.x: Along with the platypus, echidnas are the only living egg-laying mammals.

questions.q: What is the name of the process by which a caterpillar becomes a butterfly?
questions.x: Complete metamorphosis has four stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult.

questions.q: What do you call an animal that eats mainly insects?
questions.x: Anteaters, shrews, and many bats are insectivores.

questions.q: What do you call an animal that eats mainly fruit?
questions.x: Fruit bats and toucans are frugivores that help spread seeds.

questions.q: What do you call an animal that mainly eats fish?
questions.x: Pelicans, seals, and ospreys are piscivores.

questions.q: Which bird lays its eggs in other birds' nests?
questions.x: Some cuckoo chicks push the host's eggs out of the nest after hatching.

questions.q: Which snake is the longest venomous snake in the world?
questions.x: King cobras can grow to about 18 feet and mostly eat other snakes.

questions.q: What is the largest living reptile?
questions.x: Saltwater crocodiles can exceed 17 feet and live from India through Southeast Asia to northern Australia.

questions.q: What is the largest living lizard?
questions.x: Komodo dragons live on a few Indonesian islands and can grow up to about 10 feet long.

questions.q: Which amphibian can regrow lost limbs and is native to Mexico?
questions.x: Axolotls keep their larval features, like external gills, throughout their lives.

questions.q: Which group do frogs, toads, and salamanders belong to?
questions.x: The word amphibian means 'two lives', for their water and land phases.

questions.q: Which fish is known for carrying its eggs in a male's pouch?
questions.x: Male seahorses become pregnant, and may give birth to hundreds or even over a thousand young.

questions.q: Which sea creature is the largest living species of fish?
questions.x: Whale sharks can grow to over 40 feet but filter-feed on plankton.

questions.q: Which fish migrates from the ocean to rivers to spawn, often upstream?
questions.x: Many salmon return to the stream where they were born, guided partly by smell.

questions.q: Which bird of prey is known as the fastest animal in a dive?
questions.x: A peregrine falcon in a dive can exceed 200 miles per hour.

questions.q: What do bees do that helps plants reproduce?
questions.x: Bees pollinate a large share of the crops people eat, including apples and almonds.

questions.q: What do honeybees do to tell their hive-mates where flowers are?
questions.x: Karl von Frisch won a Nobel Prize for decoding the waggle dance.

questions.q: What are the three body parts of an insect?
questions.x: The thorax is where an insect's legs and wings attach.

questions.q: What is the study of birds called?
questions.x: The word comes from the Greek 'ornis', meaning bird.

questions.q: What is the study of insects called?
questions.x: There are more known species of insects than all other animal groups combined.

questions.q: What is the study of reptiles and amphibians called?
questions.x: The name comes from a Greek word meaning 'creeping thing'.

questions.q: What is the study of fish called?
questions.x: Ichthyologists study about 35,000 known fish species.

questions.q: Which bird makes the longest known annual migration, flying from pole to pole?
questions.x: Arctic terns see more daylight than any other animal, since they chase summer at both poles.

questions.q: Which butterfly is famous for migrating thousands of miles across North America?
questions.x: No single monarch makes the whole trip; it takes several generations.

questions.q: Which animal produces cube-shaped droppings?
questions.x: Their intestines have uneven elasticity, shaping the waste into cubes.

questions.q: Which mammal is covered in bony armor-like plates and can roll into a ball, found in the Americas?
questions.x: Only the three-banded armadillos can roll fully into a tight ball.

questions.q: Which scaly mammal is found in Africa and Asia and rolls up when threatened?
questions.x: Pangolins are the only mammals covered in true scales, which are made of keratin.

questions.q: What is the main food of an aardvark?
questions.x: Aardvarks use a sticky tongue that can reach about a foot into termite mounds.

questions.q: Which South American rodent is the largest rodent in the world?
questions.x: Capybaras are semi-aquatic and can weigh over 100 pounds.

questions.q: Which Australian bird is flightless and the second-tallest living bird?
questions.x: Emus can run about 30 miles per hour.

questions.q: Which flightless bird is the national symbol of New Zealand?
questions.x: A kiwi lays an egg that is about a quarter of its body weight.

questions.q: Which Arctic mammal changes its fur from brown to white in winter?
questions.x: The seasonal color change provides camouflage in snow.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a camel's hump?
questions.x: Fat in the hump can be metabolized for energy when food is scarce.

questions.q: How many humps does a Bactrian camel have?
questions.x: Dromedary camels have one hump, and Bactrian camels live in Central Asia.

questions.q: Which large African mammal spends the day in water and is often called a 'river horse'?
questions.x: The word hippopotamus comes from Greek words meaning 'river horse'.

questions.q: What is the term for animals that are cold-blooded?
questions.x: Reptiles rely on external heat, so they bask in the sun to warm up.

questions.q: What type of animal is a whale shark?
questions.x: Whale sharks are fish despite their name and filter-feed on plankton.

questions.q: What group of animals do octopuses, squid, and snails all belong to?
questions.x: Mollusks are soft-bodied animals, and many have a shell.

questions.q: To which animal group do crabs, lobsters, and shrimp belong?
questions.x: Crustaceans have jointed legs and a hard exoskeleton.

questions.q: To which animal group do starfish and sea urchins belong?
questions.x: Echinoderms typically show five-part radial symmetry.

questions.q: What is the primary diet of a blue whale?
questions.x: A blue whale can eat up to about 4 tons of krill in a day during feeding season.

questions.q: How do dolphins find food in murky water?
questions.x: Dolphins send out clicks and listen for the echoes to map their surroundings.

questions.q: What do bats use to navigate and find insects in the dark?
questions.x: Many bats can find an insect the size of a mosquito using sound alone.

questions.q: What do you call the long, sticky thread a spider makes?
questions.x: Some spiders can make several different types of silk.

questions.q: Which arachnid has a venomous curved tail stinger?
questions.x: Some scorpions glow blue-green under ultraviolet light.

questions.q: Which small feathered dinosaur, whose name means 'swift seizer', lived in Mongolia?
questions.x: Real Velociraptors were about the size of a turkey and covered in feathers.

questions.q: Which long-necked dinosaur with a whip-like tail lived in Jurassic North America?
questions.x: Diplodocus had a very long whip-like tail.

questions.q: Which armored dinosaur had a club on the end of its tail?
questions.x: Ankylosaurus was covered in bony plates and had armored eyelids.

questions.q: What event is widely believed to have ended the age of non-avian dinosaurs about 66 million years ago?
questions.x: The Chicxulub crater in Mexico marks the impact site.

questions.q: Which living animals are the direct descendants of dinosaurs?
questions.x: Birds evolved from small feathered theropod dinosaurs.

questions.q: Which prehistoric big cat is known for its enormous upper canine teeth?
questions.x: Smilodon, the saber-toothed cat, lived in the Americas until about 10,000 years ago.

questions.q: What was Megalodon?
questions.x: Megalodon lived millions of years ago and is known mostly from its huge teeth.

questions.q: Which animal was the first to be cloned from an adult cell?
questions.x: Dolly was born in 1996 at the Roslin Institute in Scotland.

questions.q: Which animal did Jane Goodall study in Tanzania?
questions.x: Goodall discovered that chimpanzees make and use tools.

questions.q: Which primate did Dian Fossey study in Rwanda?
questions.x: Fossey founded the Karisoke Research Center in Rwanda in 1967.

questions.q: Which scientist's finches in the Galapagos helped inspire his theory of natural selection?
questions.x: Darwin visited the Galapagos in 1835 aboard HMS Beagle.

questions.q: Which scientist created the system of naming species with two Latin names?
questions.x: The two-part system is called binomial nomenclature, and he published it in the 1700s.

questions.q: What is the scientific genus and species name for modern humans called?
questions.x: Homo sapiens means 'wise human' in Latin.

questions.q: What sound does a donkey make?
questions.x: A donkey's bray can be heard from miles away across open land.

questions.q: What is the term for a male bee that doesn't work and mates with the queen?
questions.x: Drones do not have stingers and die after mating.

questions.q: What is the chief food source for a mosquito's larvae?
questions.x: Only adult female mosquitoes need blood, for developing eggs.

questions.q: Which bird has the largest wingspan among living birds in the albatross family?
questions.x: The wandering albatross has a wingspan of about 11 feet and can glide for hours.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a porcupine fish inflating itself?
questions.x: Inflating makes the fish too large to swallow and raises its spines.

questions.q: What is a male duck called?
questions.x: Male ducks often have brighter plumage than females during the breeding season.

questions.q: What is a female fox called?
questions.x: A vixen typically gives birth to a litter of about four or five kits.

questions.q: What is a male swan called?
questions.x: A female swan is a pen, and pairs often stay together for many years.

questions.q: What is a female donkey called?
questions.x: A male donkey is called a jack.

questions.q: What is the name for an eagle's large nest built on a cliff or tall tree?
questions.x: Some eagles reuse and add to the same eyrie for decades.

questions.q: What is a beaver's home built in or beside a pond called?
questions.x: Beaver lodges have underwater entrances that keep predators out.

questions.q: What is a rabbit's network of underground burrows called?
questions.x: A single warren can house dozens of rabbits.

questions.q: Which big cat is the only one that lives in social groups?
questions.x: Lionesses in a pride often hunt cooperatively.

questions.q: Which deer species is unusual because both males and females grow antlers?
questions.x: Reindeer, called caribou in North America, use antlers to dig for food in snow.

questions.q: Which land mammal has the longest pregnancy, about 22 months?
questions.x: A newborn elephant calf can weigh around 200 pounds.

questions.q: How many wings does a bee have?
questions.x: A bee's front and back wings hook together in flight.

questions.q: Which animal's soft undercoat is used to make cashmere?
questions.x: Cashmere comes from the fine undercoat of cashmere goats.

questions.q: What do tadpoles use to breathe underwater?
questions.x: Tadpoles develop lungs as they turn into adult frogs.

questions.q: Which animal lives in an underground home called a sett?
questions.x: Badger setts can be used for generations and have many tunnels.

questions.q: Which snake warns enemies by shaking a tail made of loosely linked keratin segments?
questions.x: A new rattle segment is added each time the snake sheds its skin.

questions.q: Which continent is the only place emperor penguins breed in the wild?
questions.x: Emperors breed on sea ice in the harsh Antarctic winter.

questions.q: What is the home of a honeybee colony called?
questions.x: A hive can hold tens of thousands of bees in summer.

questions.q: Which desert animal stores fat, not water, in its hump?
questions.x: A camel's hump holds fat that can be turned into energy and water when food is scarce.

questions.q: What is a group of hippopotamuses called?
questions.x: A bloat of hippos can be found wallowing in rivers during the day.

questions.q: What is a group of rhinoceroses called?
questions.x: Giraffes in a group are sometimes called a tower, while rhinos form a crash.

questions.q: What is a group of zebras called?
questions.x: The dazzle of stripes may confuse predators when the herd moves.

questions.q: What is a group of jellyfish called?
questions.x: Jellyfish groups are also called blooms or swarms.

questions.q: What is a group of porcupines called?
questions.x: Prickle is the traditional collective noun for porcupines.

questions.q: What is a group of badgers called?
questions.x: Badgers live in underground burrow systems called setts.

questions.q: What is a group of foxes often called?
questions.x: A skulk or leash can describe a group of foxes, though foxes are often solitary.

questions.q: What is a group of leopards traditionally called?
questions.x: Leopards are mostly solitary, so the 'leap' is a rarely seen sight.

questions.q: What is a group of starlings that moves in swirling formations called?
questions.x: Each starling in a murmuration reacts to its nearest seven or so neighbors.

questions.q: What is a baby bat called?
questions.x: Bat pups are often born in huge colonies where mothers find them by voice and scent.

questions.q: What is a baby salmon at the stage when it is ready to migrate to the sea called?
questions.x: Salmon go through alevin, fry, parr, and smolt stages before heading to sea.

questions.q: What is a baby eel in the juvenile river stage called?
questions.x: Elvers swim upstream in great numbers after drifting across the ocean as larvae.

questions.q: What is a baby oyster that attaches to a surface called?
questions.x: Oyster spat settles on hard surfaces, often other oyster shells.

questions.q: What is the term for a baby grasshopper or dragonfly that resembles a small adult?
questions.x: Insects with incomplete metamorphosis hatch as nymphs and molt several times.

questions.q: What is a baby elephant seal or fur seal called?
questions.x: Elephant seal pups gain weight rapidly on their mother's extremely fat-rich milk.

questions.q: What is a baby turkey called?
questions.x: Turkey poults are able to leave the nest within a day of hatching.

questions.q: What is a baby crocodile or alligator called when it hatches?
questions.x: Mother crocodiles carefully carry hatchlings to the water in their mouths.

questions.q: What is the name of the pigment-containing cells that let cephalopods change color?
questions.x: Octopus and squid control thousands of chromatophores with muscles for fast color changes.

questions.q: What is the term for organs that produce light in deep-sea animals?
questions.x: Bioluminescence helps deep-sea animals find food and mates or avoid predators.

questions.q: What is a ruminant's first stomach chamber called?
questions.x: The rumen hosts microbes that ferment tough plant material.

questions.q: How many stomach chambers does a cow have?
questions.x: The chambers are the rumen, reticulum, omasum, and abomasum.

questions.q: How many neck bones (cervical vertebrae) does a giraffe have?
questions.x: Almost all mammals, including humans and giraffes, have seven neck vertebrae.

questions.q: How many chambers does a typical bird's heart have?
questions.x: Birds and mammals both have fully separated four-chambered hearts.

questions.q: How many chambers does a typical frog heart have?
questions.x: A frog has two atria and one ventricle.

questions.q: Which fish uses a bioluminescent lure on its head to attract prey in the deep sea?
questions.x: The glowing lure, called an esca, contains light-producing bacteria.

questions.q: Which marine animal is known to have no brain and no heart, yet has stinging cells called nematocysts?
questions.x: Nematocysts are tiny harpoon-like cells found across cnidarians.

questions.q: What phylum do jellyfish, corals, and sea anemones belong to?
questions.x: Cnidarians have stinging cells and radial body symmetry.

questions.q: To which phylum do sponges belong?
questions.x: Porifera means 'pore-bearing'; sponges filter water through their bodies.

questions.q: To which phylum do humans, fish, birds, and reptiles belong?
questions.x: Chordates have a notochord at some point in their development.

questions.q: To which phylum do insects, spiders, and crustaceans belong?
questions.x: Arthropods have jointed legs and an exoskeleton, and make up most known animal species.

questions.q: What group of mammals includes kangaroos, koalas, and opossums?
questions.x: Marsupials give birth to underdeveloped young that finish growing in a pouch or on the mother's body.

questions.q: What is the order that includes rabbits, hares, and pikas?
questions.x: Unlike rodents, lagomorphs have two pairs of upper incisors.

questions.q: What is the order of mammals that includes bats?
questions.x: Chiroptera means 'hand wing'.

questions.q: Which animal family do domestic cats, lions, and cheetahs belong to?
questions.x: Felidae includes about 40 living species of cats.

questions.q: Which family do wolves, foxes, and dogs belong to?
questions.x: The domestic dog is considered a subspecies of the gray wolf by many scientists.

questions.q: Which family do weasels, otters, and badgers belong to?
questions.x: Mustelids often have scent glands used for marking territory.

questions.q: Which animal is the closest living relative of whales and dolphins?
questions.x: Whales evolved from hoofed land mammals related to hippos.

questions.q: Which land animal is the closest living relative of the manatee?
questions.x: Manatees, elephants, and hyraxes are all part of the Afrotheria group.

questions.q: Which small African mammal looks like a guinea pig yet is related to elephants?
questions.x: The hyrax has foot pads that work like suction cups on rocks.

questions.q: Which male bird incubates the single egg on his feet during the Antarctic winter?
questions.x: Males fast for about two months while the females feed at sea.

questions.q: Which bird builds an elaborate bower decorated with colorful objects to attract a mate?
questions.x: Male bowerbirds arrange blue items such as bottle caps and feathers to impress females.

questions.q: Which bird can mimic chainsaws and camera shutters, native to Australia?
questions.x: A lyrebird's tail resembles an ancient lyre when displayed.

questions.q: Which wading bird is known for standing on one leg and has a pink, upside-down bill?
questions.x: Flamingos feed with their heads upside down, filtering tiny food from water.

questions.q: Which seabird dives from heights and is known for its blue feet?
questions.x: Male blue-footed boobies show off their bright feet in courtship dances.

questions.q: Which reptile has a third 'eye' on top of its head, called a parietal eye, living in New Zealand?
questions.x: The tuatara is the sole survivor of an ancient reptile order, Rhynchocephalia.

questions.q: Which giant tortoises live on islands off Ecuador and inspired Darwin's thinking?
questions.x: The Spanish word galapago means tortoise, giving the islands their name.

questions.q: Which snake kills its prey by constriction and is the heaviest snake in the world?
questions.x: Anacondas live in South America and spend much of their time in water.

questions.q: Which lizard can run on water, earning it the nickname 'Jesus lizard'?
questions.x: Basilisks can sprint across ponds on their hind legs for several feet.

questions.q: Which venomous lizard lives in the deserts of the southwestern United States?
questions.x: The Gila monster is one of only a few venomous lizards in the world.

questions.q: Which amphibian is the largest in the world, reaching about 5 feet in length?
questions.x: The Chinese giant salamander is the largest amphibian and lives in cold mountain streams.

questions.q: Which South American frog family is known for the toxins that Indigenous hunters used on blowgun darts?
questions.x: Their bright colors warn predators that they are toxic.

questions.q: What are caecilians?
questions.x: Caecilians look like worms or snakes but are amphibians.

questions.q: Which gas exchange organ does an adult frog use in addition to lungs?
questions.x: Frogs can absorb oxygen through their moist skin.

questions.q: What do archerfish use to catch insects above the water?
questions.x: Archerfish can spit a stream of water to knock insects from overhanging plants.

questions.q: Which fish cleans parasites from the skin of larger fish at 'cleaning stations'?
questions.x: Cleaner wrasses recognize returning clients and can pass mirror-like tests in studies.

questions.q: Which fish can climb onto land and breathe air through its skin, using fins to move across mud?
questions.x: Mudskippers live in mangrove swamps and tidal flats.

questions.q: Which fish species has a skeleton made entirely of cartilage?
questions.x: Rays and skates also have cartilaginous skeletons.

questions.q: What organ lets bony fish control their buoyancy?
questions.x: Sharks lack a swim bladder and use their oily livers for buoyancy.

questions.q: What sensory system lets fish detect water movement along their sides?
questions.x: The lateral line helps schooling fish stay in sync.

questions.q: Which tiny sea creature is known as the 'immortal jellyfish' for its ability to revert to a juvenile stage?
questions.x: It can return to the polyp stage under stress, in theory restarting its life cycle.

questions.q: What is the name for the pointed tooth of a narwhal?
questions.x: The tusk is a spiraled canine tooth that grows through the upper lip.

questions.q: What do baleen whales use to filter food from water?
questions.x: Baleen is made of keratin, the same protein as human fingernails.

questions.q: Which sea mammal uses rocks to crack open shellfish while floating on its back?
questions.x: Sea otters have the densest fur of any animal, with up to a million hairs per square inch.

questions.q: Which sea creature has a radula, a ribbon of tiny teeth, used for scraping food?
questions.x: Mollusks like snails and chitons use a radula for feeding.

questions.q: Which sea creature has a chewing structure called Aristotle's lantern?
questions.x: The five-toothed structure was described by Aristotle in antiquity.

questions.q: Which crustacean smashes clam shells with a lightning-fast club-like appendage?
questions.x: Mantis shrimp strikes can create cavitation bubbles that produce a shock wave.

questions.q: What is the common name for the crustacean that carries its shell home and swaps shells as it grows?
questions.x: Hermit crabs sometimes line up in order of size to swap shells.

questions.q: Which arthropod is a 'living fossil' with blue blood used in medical testing?
questions.x: Horseshoe crab blood clots in the presence of bacterial toxins, so it is used to test medical products.

questions.q: What is the sticky silk-like substance mussels use to attach to rocks?
questions.x: Byssal threads are tough protein fibers that anchor mussels in strong currents.

questions.q: What is the iridescent inner shell layer of oysters that forms pearls called?
questions.x: A pearl forms when an oyster coats an irritant with layers of nacre.

questions.q: What is the hard outer covering of an insect called?
questions.x: Insects molt to grow because their exoskeleton does not stretch.

questions.q: What do insects use to breathe, the small openings along their bodies?
questions.x: Spiracles lead to tubes called tracheae that carry oxygen throughout the body.

questions.q: Which insect spends most of its life underground as a nymph and emerges every 13 or 17 years in some species?
questions.x: The prime-number cycles may help cicadas avoid predators and parasites.

questions.q: Which insect has the shortest adult lifespan, often living less than a day?
questions.x: Some adult mayflies live only hours, just long enough to mate and lay eggs.

questions.q: How many eyes do most spiders have?
questions.x: Some spider species have six, four, or even fewer eyes, but eight is typical.

questions.q: What do you call the specialized organs spiders use to spin silk?
questions.x: Spiders have up to eight spinnerets and can produce several silk types.

questions.q: Which arachnid group includes ticks and mites?
questions.x: Acari include thousands of species and some are microscopic.

questions.q: Which group of prehistoric flying reptiles, which included Pteranodon, had wings of skin?
questions.x: Pterosaurs were the first vertebrates to evolve powered flight.

questions.q: What is the name for an extinct marine reptile with a dolphin-like body?
questions.x: Ichthyosaurs gave birth to live young in the water.

questions.q: Which period is the time when Stegosaurus and Brachiosaurus lived?
questions.x: The Jurassic ran from about 201 to 145 million years ago.

questions.q: During which period did Tyrannosaurus rex live?
questions.x: T. rex lived in North America in the Late Cretaceous, about 68 to 66 million years ago.

questions.q: Which dinosaur had a sail-like structure on its back and may have been semi-aquatic?
questions.x: Spinosaurus had a crocodile-like snout and was likely a fish eater.

questions.q: Which duck-billed dinosaur had a long hollow crest on its head?
questions.x: The crest may have helped it make loud, low calls.

questions.q: What are fossilized dinosaur droppings called?
questions.x: Coprolites reveal details about prehistoric diets.

questions.q: What are the stones swallowed by some dinosaurs and birds to help grind food called?
questions.x: Modern birds like chickens swallow grit for the same purpose.

questions.q: Which small feathered dinosaur found in China had four wings?
questions.x: Microraptor had long flight feathers on both its arms and legs.

questions.q: Which famous early bird-like fossil from Germany was found in Jurassic limestone in 1861?
questions.x: Archaeopteryx had feathers like a bird but also teeth and a bony tail like a dinosaur.

questions.q: What was the giant flightless bird that lived in New Zealand and was hunted to extinction by about 1400?
questions.x: The largest moa stood about 12 feet tall with its neck stretched.

questions.q: Which island was the home of the dodo?
questions.x: The dodo disappeared within about a century after Europeans arrived in the late 1500s.

questions.q: What is the mother-offspring bond called when a duckling follows the first moving thing it sees?
questions.x: Konrad Lorenz made imprinting famous with his goslings that followed him.

questions.q: Which scientist shared a Nobel Prize in 1973 for work on animal behavior including imprinting in geese?
questions.x: He shared the prize with Niko Tinbergen and Karl von Frisch.

questions.q: Which insect did Thomas Hunt Morgan use to show that genes are carried on chromosomes?
questions.x: Morgan's fruit fly work showed that genes are carried on chromosomes.

questions.q: Which dog became the first animal to orbit Earth, aboard Sputnik 2 in 1957?
questions.x: Laika flew aboard Sputnik 2 in November 1957.

questions.q: Which chimpanzee was the first great ape in space, launched by NASA in 1961?
questions.x: Ham flew on a Mercury-Redstone mission and returned safely.

questions.q: Which African gray parrot, studied by Irene Pepperberg, learned to use words in context?
questions.x: Alex could identify colors, shapes, and quantities.

questions.q: Which gorilla was taught a modified form of sign language by Francine Patterson?
questions.x: Koko reportedly learned more than 1,000 signs.

questions.q: Which organ in the roof of a snake's mouth helps it analyze scents collected by its tongue?
questions.x: The forked tongue delivers scent particles to this organ, giving a snake a kind of directional smell.

questions.q: What is the name of the reflective layer behind a cat's retina that makes its eyes glow in the dark?
questions.x: The layer reflects light back through the retina, boosting night vision.

questions.q: What is the part of a bird's body that stores food before it is digested?
questions.x: Pigeons also use their crop to make 'crop milk' for their chicks.

questions.q: What is a bird's voice organ, located where the windpipe splits, called?
questions.x: The syrinx lets songbirds produce two different notes at once.
